# Compatibility implementation throughput

Use `cluster.py` on both retained full result inventories. Groups represent first observed blockers, not promised pass gains.

1. Implement shared owners in Rust, then test values, metadata, ordering, errors and real I/O against both pinned Node and latest stable.
2. During edits, run the affected API test first. Run all API/shared/framework checks once the focused behavior passes.
3. Reuse unchanged Core qualification with source proof for Node-only edits. The iteration profile shares unwind dependencies with tests; production release panic behavior is unchanged.
4. Freeze qualified binaries before complete fixed-budget sweeps; retain failures, fixture restoration and resource evidence. Never infer full counts from selected successes.
5. Prioritize missing shared foundations: HTTP/2 server operations dominate missing-callable call sites; Worker support and stream/iter are separate large absent families. TLS transport/session ownership and HTTPS reuse can unlock multiple related families. Complete real behavior rather than exposing empty API shapes.

Latest stable oracle: verified official Node v26.12.0, matching full source outside the Quench package boundary. Its own official suite baseline has 16 failures, retained separately from Quench failures.

Focused tests that spawn `process.execPath` need both `quench-node` and `run-parallel` rebuilt from the same library. `cargo test` alone refreshes its declared runner but can leave the sibling `quench-node` stale. A paired `cargo build --profile iteration -p quench-node -p quench-node-test --bin quench-node --bin run-parallel -j2` reuses the same library artifacts and avoids false child-process regressions. Run full API tests with `--nocapture` so the first failure is visible immediately.

Keep Blob/File lazy initialization separate from Fetch: importing buffer must not recursively initialize undici while the caller's Buffer lexical binding is in its temporal dead zone. Share canonical Blob/File exports without eager Fetch work.
